<div class="section-intro">
Marine quantitative ecologist and fisheries scientist working across ecological modelling, stock assessment, marine data science, population dynamics, and reproducible scientific computing.
</div>

**Measure change. Model uncertainty. Inform fisheries decisions.**

I connect ecological theory, marine observations, statistical modelling, and reproducible computing to understand changing populations and fisheries. My main study system is the Humboldt Current, with particular emphasis on pelagic fish and Peruvian anchovy.

## Research

My work focuses on translating ecological and fisheries observations into quantitative evidence that can support interpretation, assessment, and decision-making in dynamic marine systems.

### Population dynamics and stock assessment

Recruitment, growth, selectivity, demographic structure, uncertainty, model diagnostics, and management-oriented assessment.

### Spatio-temporal marine ecology

Habitat, distribution shifts, accessibility, hotspots, fleet behaviour, and spatial and spatio-temporal models.

### Environmental variability and ecosystem responses

Oceanographic and climatic drivers, ecosystem regimes, pressure-state relationships, and responses of pelagic populations to environmental variability.

### Statistical ecology and scientific computing

Hierarchical, additive, multivariate, machine-learning, and reproducible modelling workflows implemented primarily in R, Python, and related scientific computing tools.
